citation.title: Operational stability and beam transport constraints in long-pulse neutral beam injection on KSTAR
citation.authors: J.H. Jeong, S.C. Hong, B.S. Kim, J.Y. Jang, W. Cho, J.G. Kwak, S.J. Wang

topic: KSTAR NBI long-pulse beam transport: perveance drift, re-ionization and stray-field deflection
own_question: Which beam-transport constraints reduce effective neutral beam power in discharges longer than 100 s?
actual_method_and_evidence: The authors compare two discharges (#21757 degraded, #34705 stable) using water-flow calorimetry, duct thermocouples, beam-duct pressure, a neutron-scaling estimate of delivered neutral beam power, and a simplified COMSOL trajectory calculation. They describe the results as qualitative and not causally established. The paper contains no CES, Ti, BES/ECEI, or nowcasting content.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not relevant. There are no CES reports, report timing, or nowcasting targets.
validation_if_relevant: Two-shot qualitative comparison. There is no statistical or held-out validation.
forbidden_inferences: That NBI power variation affects CES label quality in our dataset
Any information about CES reporting latency
That the 2022 campaign shots or the chord we use are discussed
That stray-field re-ionization is an established mechanism
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Exclude. The paper is NBI engineering and does not address CES temperature, impurity versus main-ion Ti, BES/ECEI, or causal estimation. At most, it could serve as a generic reference that KSTAR NBI power can vary within a pulse. That use is not needed and could invite unsupported links to CES beam-dependent measurements, which this paper does not examine.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
